articles.title: Simon Raises 2026 Expectations as Leasing, Development Pipeline Accelerate
articles.narrative: Simon Property Group, the nation's largest mall owner, reported strong second-quarter results for 2026, with climbing revenue, funds from operations (FFO), and tenant sales, leading the company to raise its full-year outlook. The REIT signed over 1,200 leases totaling more than 4.8 million square feet, with new deals increasing 20% year-over-year and initial base rents on new deals up 17%. Occupancy at its U.S. malls and premium outlets remained at 96%, while base minimum rent increased 6.3% to $62.42 per square foot. The company is also accelerating its development pipeline, with $1.07 billion in projects underway and an additional $600 million expected to start construction in the second half of the year, bringing the total pipeline to over $4 billion.

data_points.project_notes: Simon took on approximately 1 million square feet of bankruptcy-related space during the quarter, largely from Saks Off 5th, and has already re-leased about half of that space.

articles.title: Law Firm Greenberg Traurig Takes 25K SF at Related Ross Dev in West Palm
articles.narrative: Law firm Greenberg Traurig has signed a 10-year lease for approximately 25,000 square feet at the under-construction 15 CityPlace office development in West Palm Beach, FL. The firm will occupy the entire 12th floor of the 25-story building, with a move-in planned for fall 2027. This relocation signifies the firm's long-term commitment to the West Palm Beach market and its strategy to accommodate growing client demand.

data_points.project_notes: The building is part of a larger development by Related Ross, which secured a $772 million construction debt package in 2025. The building is expected to span about 500,000 square feet.

articles.title: Law Firm Dunn Isaacson Rhee Leases 11K SF at 7 World Trade Center

The landlord, Silverstein Properties, noted that 7 World Trade Center continues to attract leading firms seeking high-quality workplaces that reflect their brand and support their employees and clients.

articles.title: Alliance for Downtown New York Inks 14K SF at 42 Broadway
articles.narrative: The Alliance for Downtown New York, a nonprofit managing Lower Manhattan's business improvement district, has expanded its presence by signing a 14,420-square-foot lease at 42 Broadway in the Financial District. The organization plans to relocate its operations division to the new space, while its corporate headquarters will remain at 120 Broadway. The landlord, Cammeby's International Group, confirmed the transaction, noting that the space is currently under construction.
articles.market_intelligence: Office asking rents in Lower Manhattan averaged $61.91 per square foot in July.

articles.title: New York’s Rent Freeze Was Only An Aftershock. This 2019 Law Was The Quake.
articles.narrative: This article argues that New York's Housing Stability and Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (HSTPA) is the primary cause of financial distress for owners of rent-stabilized properties, leading to an increase in vacant, uninhabitable units. The law eliminated landlords' ability to raise rents to market rates after a tenant vacates, making it uneconomical to invest in necessary repairs for units that often require significant upgrades after long-term tenancies. While the recent rent freeze exacerbated the situation, the 2019 law fundamentally altered the financial viability of maintaining these properties, forcing owners to keep units offline rather than incur unrecoverable renovation costs. This situation contributes to a reduction in available housing stock despite some recent gains in the overall number of rent-stabilized units.

articles.title: BLS: U.S. Economy Unexpectedly Loses 23,000 Jobs in July
articles.narrative: The U.S. economy unexpectedly lost 23,000 nonfarm jobs in July, a significant deviation from the 83,000 gain forecasted by economists. This decline was compounded by downward revisions to May and June's job figures, totaling 103,000 fewer jobs. Despite the job losses, the unemployment rate slightly decreased to 4.1 percent, primarily due to a shrinking labor force. Sector-wise, healthcare continued to add jobs, albeit at a slower pace, while retail trade and financial activities experienced notable declines.

articles.title: Eldridge Capital Provides $278M Loan for Refinancing of Midtown Atlanta Office Tower
articles.narrative: Eldridge Capital Management has provided a $278 million refinancing loan for Ten Twenty Spring, a 540,000-square-foot office tower in Midtown Atlanta. The 25-story building, owned by Portman and Blackstone Real Estate, was delivered in 2024 and serves as an anchor for the larger Spring Quarter mixed-use development. The tower boasts a strong tenant mix, including a financial institution establishing its corporate headquarters there, and offers extensive amenities.

data_points.notable_features: 25-story tower with floor-to-ceiling windows, 360-degree panoramic views, indoor-outdoor bar, rooftop Japanese dining, private office terraces, coworking lounge, historic gardens, ground-floor retail, and connectivity to MARTA Midtown station.
data_points.project_notes: Anchors Portman's Spring Quarter mixed-use development.

articles.title: Berkadia Arranges $19.1M in Acquisition Financing for Build-to-Rent Community in St. Cloud, Florida
articles.narrative: Berkadia has secured $19.1 million in acquisition financing for Ibis Park at Harmony West, a newly built, build-to-rent residential community in St. Cloud, Florida. The financing was arranged for Bayshore Investment Partners, which acquired the property from D.R. Horton for $29.4 million. The five-year, fixed-rate loan includes a full-term, interest-only structure.

data_points.address: 7110 Sandhill Crane Way, St. Cloud, FL

articles.title: Fairfield Residential Completes 340-Unit Multifamily Project in Houston’s Montrose District
articles.narrative: Fairfield Residential has completed 1010 Waugh, a 340-unit multifamily project in Houston's Montrose district. The 14-story building offers a variety of unit types with modern finishes and a comprehensive amenity package, including a pool, fitness center, and coworking spaces.

data_points.notable_features: Units feature stainless steel appliances, quartz countertops, and in-unit washers/dryers. Amenities include a pool, fitness center, golf simulator, sky lounge, coworking space, conference rooms, and a game room.

articles.title: KBS closes sale of seven-building business campus in Plano
articles.narrative: KBS has completed the sale of Tollway North Office Park, a seven-building Class-A business campus in Plano, TX, to BH Properties. The 297,591-square-foot property is located within the Legacy Business Park, a premier business destination in the Dallas-Fort Worth metro area. The transaction underscores the continued investor interest in well-located assets within this high-growth market, driven by strong population and employment gains.

data_points.notable_features: Seven-building Class-A business campus with dedicated exterior suite entrances, 10- to 13-foot finished ceilings, and above-market parking ratio.

articles.title: Stream Realty Partners closes 56,256-square-foot office lease in Houston
articles.narrative: Stream Realty Partners represented Superior Energy Services, Inc. in a 56,256-square-foot office lease for its new corporate headquarters at 8020 Katy Freeway in Houston. The relocation from Downtown Houston to the Spring Branch submarket provides a more central location and improved connectivity for the company's long-term business objectives.

data_points.notable_features: LEED-certified Class A office building with immediate access to Interstate 10.

articles.title: Lenexa’s Henderson Companies adds pair of leaders in venue sector
articles.narrative: Henderson Companies, the parent company of Henderson Engineers and Henderson Building Solutions, has appointed two new leaders within its venue sector, which focuses on the design and construction of large-scale, multipurpose facilities across the nation. Bridget Lowe has been hired as convention center practice director, bringing 15 years of industry experience to oversee client experience, technical quality, innovation, business development, and employee engagement. Additionally, Jason Kartak has been promoted to entertainment practice director, where he will lead the firm's entertainment practice, specializing in performing arts centers, amphitheaters, and other immersive environments, leveraging his more than 30 years of industry experience.

articles.title: Venture One Real Estate acquires 131,998-square-foot industrial portfolio in Chicago market
articles.narrative: Venture One Real Estate, through its VK Industrial VII, LP fund, has acquired a three-building industrial portfolio totaling 131,998 square feet across the Chicago metropolitan area. The portfolio was fully occupied at the time of closing, featuring a mix of single and multi-tenant properties with strong tenant demand for industrial space in the market.

articles.title: High Street Residential Tops Out on First Manhattan Development
articles.narrative: High Street Residential, the residential arm of Trammell Crow Company, has topped out construction on The Marq, a 25-story luxury residential tower in Manhattan's SoHo neighborhood. This marks the firm's inaugural development in Manhattan, with completion anticipated in the fourth quarter of 2027. The project will feature 99 residential units, including 25 affordable apartments, and ground-floor retail space. The development aims to capture the vibrant and elegant character of SoHo, leveraging its desirable location near transit hubs and green spaces.

data_points.address: 126 Lafayette St., New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Includes 25 affordable apartments; units range from studios to three-bedroom penthouses. Located near major transit hubs and Hudson River Park.
data_points.project_notes: This is High Street Residential's first Manhattan development.

articles.title: MMCC Arranges Financing for Riverside County Self-Storage Property
articles.narrative: Marcus & Millichap Capital Corporation (MMCC) has arranged $7.38 million in financing for Beaumont RV and Self Storage, a 49,958-square-foot self-storage facility in Beaumont, CA. The 10-year loan, secured through a national federal credit union, features a 5.75% interest rate and a 30-year amortization period. This financing reflects the continued strong demand for self-storage, driven by its durable operating fundamentals and the need for flexible storage solutions for both household and recreational uses.

data_points.notable_features: Offers traditional self-storage units and dedicated RV and boat storage; located near Interstate 10.
data_points.project_notes: The loan has a 10-year term, 5.75% interest rate, and 30-year amortization period.

articles.title: 3650 Capital Furnishes Construction Loan for Yonkers Self-Storage
articles.narrative: 3650 Capital has provided a $24 million senior construction loan for the completion of a 949-unit self-storage development in Yonkers, NY. The project, sponsored by Cayre Equities and KCT Inc., will be branded and operated by CubeSmart. This financing structure allowed the sponsors to emerge from a court-supervised reorganization, resolve outstanding claims, and accelerate project completion in a supply-constrained market.

data_points.notable_features: Will be branded and operated by CubeSmart.
data_points.project_notes: Financing provided as exit capital concurrent with the borrower's emergence from a court-supervised reorganization. Loan features a 36-month initial term with one six-month extension option.
